text:
carla: Quick sync — I put together acceptance criteria for the per-route/tiered tail-handling policy we discussed. want to lock these before i drop into the PRD.

ben: sharing now. main ask from sales: per-customer SLO overrides for paid tiers, and clear fallback behavior when error budget depleted.

carla: +1. current draft goals: 1) per-route 95/99 latency SLOs, 2) shared error budgets with per-tenant caps, 3) graceful degrade to lower-cost model or cached prefix when budget burned, 4) rollout canary by % of traffic.

alice: a couple infra notes: tail spikes are usually due to KV cache misses + long sequences. for degrade path we should support a ‘shorten-context’ mode + kv-prefetch TTL bump. implementation risk: opens cold-start regressions.

carla: good call. add acceptance criteria: degrade path must not increase median latency by >5ms and must reduce p99 by at least 30% for affected requests.

dave: error budget math question — are we doing global budget per-customer or per-route? engineering preference is per-route with a global cap to avoid noisy neighbors. example: route A gets 70% of customer budget, rest shared.

emma: customers expect deterministic behavior: if we say "degrade at X% burn" they want a hard threshold and notification. CS needs webhooks or console alerts + human readable reason.

carla: noted. draft policy snippet (for PRD):
```json
{
  "route": "chat.completion",
  "slo": {"p95_ms": 120, "p99_ms": 300},
  "budget": {"monthly_tokens": 1000000, "per_route_cap_pct": 0.7},
  "degrade": [
    {"when": "p99 > 2x_slo OR budget_burn > 80%", "action": "fallback:model.lite"},
    {"when": "budget_burn > 95%", "action": "reject_with_429_or_queue"}
  ],
  "notifications": {"webhook": true, "console": true}
}
```

ben: solid. only ask: add an explicit timeline and rollout gates in acceptance criteria. we should require 2-weeks canary at 5% traffic with +observability hooks before any customer-facing tier changes.

alice: agree. also need automated regression test that simulates long-sequence traffic + KV miss pattern. i can add a toy harness in eng-runtime repo.

carla: acceptance checklist (proposed):
- [ ] SLO definitions per-route (p95/p99) documented
- [ ] Error budget allocation algorithm documented and example cases
- [ ] Degrade actions implemented (fallback, shorten-context, reject)
- [ ] Canary rollout plan: 2w at 5% then 1w at 25% then GA
- [ ] Observability: cost+latency per token, per-route, per-tenant
- [ ] CS webhooks + console messaging for degrade events
- [ ] Regression harness and load tests

dave: edge cases: bursty traffic from many small tenants could burn shared budget rapidly. suggest add min-guarantee for small-tenants so customers on free tier aren't completely killed.

emma: +1 on min-guarantee. also need docs/FAQ text for customers explaining what fallback models mean for quality. CS will draft.

carla: decisions needed from product:
1) per-route vs per-tenant primary budget? (recommend per-route with global cap)
2) degrade priority: prefer fallback model over outright rejects for paid tiers?
3) notification surface: webhook + console + email for enterprise only?

ben: my votes: 1) per-route primary, 2) fallback for paid tiers, reject/queue for free, 3) webhook+console for all, email for enterprise.

alice: technical blocker we should flag: fallback model must be quantized variant available in same region to avoid cross-region latency. will add to PRD.

carla: thanks all. next steps: i'll update the PRD with these acceptance criteria and the policy snippet, file the RFC, and tag runtime + SRE owners. pls react with :thumbsup: if you agree or comment if not.

infra-bot: RFC created: rfc/2026-tiered-tail-handling. assigned: @alice @dave. link: https://rfc.internal/r/2026-tiered-tail-handling

ben: :thumbsup:

alice: :thumbsup: i'll start the harness PR today.

emma: will draft CS FAQ and a short email template for enterprise alerts.

carla: great — closing thread, will ping reviewers on PRD.
